inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation $32.460M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $7.177M (financing). JKHY publishes no combined equity-award figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: 70.11M basic shares outstanding on the 10-K cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-08-12) plus 0.18M dilutive RSUs (FY2026 incremental shares 177k) = 70.3M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. FY2026 buybacks of $448.2M (2.947M shares at ~$152 avg) took the count from 73.0M to 70.3M; the flat count is funded by a repurchaser with a 5.46M-share remaining authorisation.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-28T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 121.04-193.39
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 10y UST ~4.2% (Sep 2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.8 (low-beta, recurring-revenue processor: ~90% of revenue is recurring processing/support, 5-7 year contracts) gives cost of equity ~8.2%; debt is a $40M revolver against a $10.4B market cap, so WACC rounds to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases. Operating lease cost ($11.0M FY2026) is inside operating expenses, so EBITDA and EBIT are already after lease cost; the $37.8M lease liability is therefore NOT added to net debt. Charged once, in the flows.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Interest income of $23.1M (FY2026) is left in place and NOT stripped: net debt is +$27.9M (no net cash pile to double count), and the component build starts from operating income, which excludes net interest (+$17.8M pre-tax) entirely. The income appears to arise from payments-settlement float rather than a treasury cash balance.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company: tech/SaaS'), 10-year horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping with EBITDA margin expansion. JKHY is a US bank/credit-union core-processing and fintech company (Core, Payments, Complementary, Corporate Services segments; ~7,500 FI clients) with ~90% recurring revenue. No prior DCF, no memory entry, no Analysis JSON at build time (being generated in parallel): qualitative context is from the FY2026 10-K, the 2026-08-18 Q4 FY26 press release and the analyst's own knowledge of the company. THREE THINGS THE HEADLINE NUMBERS HIDE: (1) The Metrics CSV 'CapEx' column ($67.1M) is PP&E only. JKHY also capitalises software development ($184.2M FY2026, 7.2% of revenue) and purchased software ($4.1M); the company's own FCF definition deducts both, so total capex is $255.4M = 10.0% of revenue and the CSV FreeCashFlow column ($694.9M) is overstated by ~$188M. (2) FY2026 cash taxes paid were $38.9M against $150.0M of tax expense (current federal tax expense $2.7M; deferred federal expense $117.3M; deferred tax liability up $126M). This is the OBBBA (July 2025) restoration of immediate Section 174 R&D expensing letting the previously capitalised 2022-24 R&D be deducted at once -- a one-off ~$111M cash benefit that reverses the FY2023 hit (tax paid $145.9M vs $107.9M expense). The forward cash tax rate is set at 22.5% (FY2026 effective rate 23.0%, FY2025 22.2%, modest ongoing timing benefit from expensing a growing capitalised-software base). (3) Deferred contract costs (implementation and commission costs capitalised under ASC 340-40) are a structural cash drag: net increase $115.6M FY24, $50.9M FY25, $85.5M FY26 against revenue increases of $138M/$160M/$169M -- modelled as wc_capture -40% of the YoY revenue change. RESULT: reported_fcf $539.4M is the company definition (OCF 762.0 - PP&E 67.1 - software 188.4 + asset-sale proceeds 32.8); last_fcf $499.8M is that less SBC incl. equity taxes; owner_fcf_normalised $355.9M strips the $32.8M one-off asset-sale proceeds and the ~$111.1M tax-timing benefit and is the figure the year-1 projection should be judged against (year-1 base owner FCF ~$395M is a 6% growth year on a 14% normalised margin, not a 21% collapse from $500M). Owner-FCF margin history on the same basis: FY16 14.8, FY17 15.1, FY18 16.5, FY19 15.1, FY20 18.4, FY21 15.7, FY22 14.6, FY23 6.6 (Section 174 hit plus deferred-cost swing), FY24 13.6, FY25 15.8, FY26 18.3 reported / 14.0 normalised. Also: FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS is $6.98 per the press release and XBRL diluted count; the Metrics CSV carries 7.00. Deconversion revenue was $42.8M in FY2026 (guided $23M for FY2027, the company's floor convention), which is why GAAP guidance (+5.5-6.5%) trails non-GAAP adjusted growth (+6.3-7.3%).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 GAAP revenue guidance midpoint (+6.0%; range $2,684-2,709M). The through-cycle anchor is the 7.7% revenue 5-yr CAGR; the equity CAGR (9.2%) is the method's default but is distorted by the $448M FY2026 buyback (equity fell $79M in FY26 while net income was $503M) and EPS CAGRs (11%) embed margin expansion and buybacks that a revenue path must not double count.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs run FY2021->FY2026 (5-yr) and FY2023->FY2026 (3-yr), fiscal years to 30 June. EPS uses GAAP diluted $4.12 -> $5.03 -> $6.98. FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (OCF - PP&E capex - capitalised and purchased software - SBC - equity-award taxes), TAX-NORMALISED for the Section 174 timing swing: FY2021 $275.8M -> FY2026 $355.9M gives 5.2% (the reported-basis owner FCF $466.9M gives 11.1%, inflated by the $111M one-off tax benefit); the 3-yr 26.6% is a recovery off the FY2023 trough ($175.5M normalised) and is not a run-rate. Owner-FCF growth (5.2%) trailing revenue growth (7.7%) over five years says the incremental dollar of revenue has cost more in capitalised software (5.5% -> 7.2% of revenue) and deferred onboarding costs than the margin expansion has returned -- the JH Platform / public-cloud build is being paid for now. SBC is small and stable (1.2-1.6% of revenue) and is not the reason.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = FY2027 GAAP guidance midpoint (+6.0%; deconversion revenue steps down $43M -> $23M, masking ~6.8% underlying). Years 2-4 at 6-6.5% reflect the record 58 competitive core wins in FY2026 (14 above $1B assets) converting to revenue over the 12-24 month implementation lag, then a glide to 3% as bank/CU consolidation (~3%/yr fewer institutions) caps the addressable base.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin was 31.1/32.6/33.3% in FY24/25/26. Year 1 33.2% = FY2027 guided GAAP operating margin midpoint 24.6% plus 8.6% D&A (management flagged tough H1 comparisons and the lower deconversion contribution). Thereafter +30bp/yr, the cadence management has delivered on adjusted operating margin, plateauing at 35% from year 7 (~26.4% operating margin) as public-cloud hosting mix and Banno/payments scale.
base.capex_rationale: Total capex = PP&E ($67M) + capitalised software ($184M) + purchased software ($4M) = 10.0% of FY2026 revenue. Tapers to 9.0% only from year 3 as the JH Platform core build passes its 2025-27 investment peak; D&A held at 8.6% (amortisation is catching up with the capitalised base: $171M FY26, $163M scheduled for FY27 before new additions).
base.narrative: Steady compounder: mid-single-digit growth, 30bp/yr margin expansion, flat share count.

bull.narrative: JH Platform wins larger FIs, payments (faster payments +47%, card +6%) and Banno compound; growth returns to the 7.7% five-year trend and above, margin reaches 37% EBITDA.

bear.narrative: Bank/CU consolidation and Fiserv/FIS pricing erode the client base faster than wins replace it; public-cloud migration and platform capex stay at 10% of revenue with no margin payoff; cap multiple 15x for a structurally slower business.

scenario_narratives.base: Jack Henry keeps doing what it has done for a decade: 6-7% underlying revenue growth from a ~7,500-institution base that is shrinking ~3%/yr by count but growing in assets per client, with wallet share rising through Banno digital, card and faster-payments (PayCenter/FedNow/RTP) attach, and private-to-public cloud hosting migration. Year 1 follows FY2027 guidance (GAAP +5.5-6.5%, operating margin 24.5-24.7%, EPS $7.33-7.38); years 2-4 lift to 6-6.5% as the record FY2026 core-win cohort (58 competitive wins, 14 above $1B in assets) goes live. EBITDA margin expands 30bp/yr to 35% by year 7 as hosting mix and scale offset personnel inflation; capitalised software eases from 7.2% toward 6% of revenue after the JH Platform build peaks; deferred onboarding costs keep absorbing ~40% of each incremental revenue dollar. Owner-FCF margin rises from ~14.5% to ~17.5%. Buybacks hold the count flat; the dividend (~$2.40/share, 34% payout) is inside the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The JH Platform (cloud-native, componentised core) becomes the default replacement core for $1-50B community and regional institutions that Fiserv and FIS are losing on service, and the FY2026 win rate is the start of a share-gain cycle rather than a peak. Growth runs 7-8% for four years (back to and above the 7.7% five-year CAGR), faster payments and card processing add Payments-segment mix (already the largest segment at ~37% of revenue, ~44% segment margin), Banno active users keep compounding at double digits, and public-cloud hosting lifts gross margin. EBITDA margin reaches 37% (operating margin ~28%) with capex falling to 8.5% of revenue as the platform build completes. Capital returns continue at the FY2026 pace ($448M buybacks on a stock the company itself judged cheap at $140-152).
scenario_narratives.bear: Consolidation is the axis: US bank and credit-union counts fall 3-4%/yr, and the acquirers are disproportionately on Fiserv/FIS/in-house cores, so deconversion income becomes attrition without replacement. Fiserv's post-2025 pricing aggression on renewals and neo-core entrants (Finxact/Fiserv, Alkami/Q2 on digital, nCino on lending) cap price. Growth fades to 2.5-3%, margin slips to 32% EBITDA as the public-cloud migration raises hosting cost without a price offset, capitalised software stays at 10% of revenue with capex above D&A indefinitely, and the market re-rates the business as a low-growth processor (15x terminal cap). No solvency question -- net debt is $28M -- so the bear case is a value trap, not a distress case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the house 15/50/35 to 20/55/25. Bear up to 20%: industry consolidation is a slow but certain secular headwind and the FY26 owner-FCF growth (5.2% 5-yr, tax-normalised) already trails revenue growth, showing the platform build is costing real cash. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs the JH Platform to win share from Fiserv/FIS at scale, which has not yet lifted growth above the 7-8% band in any year since FY2019 -- a single unproven driver. Base at 55%: 50 years of uninterrupted revenue growth, ~90% recurring revenue, 5-7 year contracts and guidance that has been met or beaten make the middle path unusually well anchored.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Jack Henry as a stream of owner free cash flow after fully expensing SBC and after treating capitalised software development ($184M, 7.2% of revenue) and deferred onboarding costs as the real reinvestment they are. The FY2026 base year must be normalised: strip the ~$111M Section 174 cash-tax timing benefit and the $32.8M asset-sale proceeds, which together turn the company's 108% FCF-to-net-income conversion into ~71% on an owner basis. The result is a low-risk compounder whose fair value rests on 6% growth compounding into 30bp/yr of margin expansion for a decade; at an 8% WACC and a 20x terminal cap the base case lands near the current price, and the 15% hurdle entry price sits well below it, as it should for a business the market discounts at ~8%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Bank/credit-union consolidation: ~3%/yr fewer institutions; client losses via M&A are only partly offset by deconversion fees (FY26 $42.8M, guided down to $23M).
Competitive pricing on core renewals from Fiserv/FIS and digital-first entrants (Alkami, Q2, nCino); the record FY2026 win rate may be a cyclical peak.
JH Platform / public-cloud migration: capitalised software has risen from 5.5% to 7.2% of revenue; if the base case taper to 9% total capex does not occur, ~$25M/yr of owner FCF is lost by year 10.
Cash tax normalisation: FY2026 cash taxes were 6% of pre-tax income; the model assumes 22.5% from year 1. Any reader anchoring on FY2026 OCF ($762M) overstates the run-rate by ~$110M.
Margin expansion cadence: management guided FY2027 GAAP operating margin DOWN (24.5-24.7% vs 25.0%) on tough H1 comparisons; the base case assumes the 30bp/yr expansion resumes from year 2.
Deferred contract costs: the -40% working-capital capture is an average of three volatile years (-84%, -32%, -51% of the revenue increase); a return to FY2024's rate would cut owner FCF by ~$70M/yr.
Terminal value is ~65% of enterprise value at a 20x cap; at 15x the base value falls roughly a fifth.
